doc.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023

chapter: Women in jazz and the business
title: Teaching recording and technology; home recording for film scores
summary: Bailey encourages students to learn technology and notes remote file-based recording; she learns gear from them.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Um hum. And do your students ask you about that part of the guitar world? About the technology available? Actually I’m going to re-phrase that question to include do you encourage them to learn Finale and all the technology that is out there to record at home etcetera?

Yeah. Well definitely. I mean Berklee has all that stuff, and for sure. I mean I think the thing about home recording, and you know the way people are scoring now is even just transferring files and people record it at home you know. So you might play on a film score and you just send the files via Dropbox and you’ve never even met the producer person. So I mean this is a big thing. And definitely for guitar players, it is a thing to be able to have the right sound for the gig. You know? But I learn a lot from them because they’re always up on, you know, what the latest gear is so I’m always trading stuff with them too.
